name: Jess E. Ketcham
occupation: Administrator for the Wyoming State Budget Department; Laramie County commissioner-elect taking office in January 2027 (Wyoming Tribune Eagle, May 26 and Nov. 3, 2026)
education: Cheyenne East High School; attended Laramie County Community College and then the University of Wyoming, graduating with a degree in agriculture business (Wyoming Tribune Eagle, May 26, 2026)
prior_offices: Laramie County Community College Board of Trustees (about a decade, including service described by the Wyoming Tribune Eagle as including a turn as the top vote-getter in a later trustee election)
background: Jess E. Ketcham is a Laramie County commissioner-elect and takes office in January 2027. The Wyoming Tribune Eagle reported in May 2026 that he is a fifth-generation Wyomingite whose family connection to the area dates to an 1867 homestead, that he grew up in Cheyenne, graduated from East High School, attended LCCC, and graduated from the University of Wyoming with a degree in agriculture business, and that he serves as administrator for the Wyoming State Budget Department. The paper reported that he has served about a decade as an LCCC trustee, including after receiving the most votes in a later trustee general election, and that his father served as a county commissioner for around 28 years. He lost a 2024 race for the county commission by nearly 300 votes, according to that article, and in 2026 finished first among the commissioner candidates in the November 3 general election. Incumbent Commissioner Linda Heath, who lost the 2026 Republican primary, serves through the current term.
